title: Present Simple
source: original, authored for NORA; Somali needs native review
somali: Present Simple waxaa loo isticmaalaa caadooyin, hawlo joogto ah iyo xaqiiqooyin (tusaale: "Maalin kasta waan shaqeeyaa"). Marka mawduucu yahay he/she/it, verb-ka ku dar -s ama -es. Af-Soomaaliga ma laha -s sidaas oo kale, sidaa darteed ardayda badan way iloobaan.
explanation: Use it for habits, routines and facts. Add -s/-es for he, she, it. Use do/does for negatives and questions.
formula: Subject + verb (+s/es for he/she/it). Negative: do/does + not + verb. Question: Do/Does + subject + verb?

affirmative: She drinks tea in the morning.
The sun rises in the east.
Qorraxdu waxay ka soo baxdaa bari.
question: Do you speak English?
Ingiriisi ma ku hadashaa?
Does she work here?
Ma halkan bay ka shaqaysaa?
wh: What time does the shop open?

examples: I work every day.
She drinks tea in the morning.
The sun rises in the east.
mistakesSo: “He” marka subject yahay, Present Simple falka “work” wuxuu noqdaa “works”.

title: Present Continuous
source: original, authored for NORA; Somali needs native review
somali: Present Continuous wuxuu sheegayaa wax hadda socda ama qorshe dhow. Hab-dhismeedku waa am/is/are + verb-ka oo lagu daray -ing. Ardayda Soomaaliyeed badanaa waxay illoobaan am/is/are ("I going" waa khalad).
explanation: Use it for actions happening now and for near-future plans. Use am/is/are + verb-ing.
formula: Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing. Negative: am/is/are + not + verb-ing. Question: Am/Is/Are + subject + verb-ing?
examples: I am eating.
She is reading a book.
They are playing football.
mistakesSo: Present Continuous wuxuu u baahan yahay “am” marka subject-ku yahay “I”: “I am going”.
“She” waxaa la socda “is” ka hor falka -ing: “She is reading”.

title: Present Perfect
source: original, authored for NORA; Somali needs native review
somali: Present Perfect wuxuu isku xiraa wakhtigii hore iyo hadda: wax hore u dhacay laakiin saamaynta ama waayo-aragnimadu hadda taal. Hab-dhismeedku waa have/has + verb-ka qaybtiisa saddexaad (past participle). Ha ku darin wakhti dhammaaday sida "yesterday".
explanation: Use it for experiences, recent results and situations that continue to now. Have/has + past participle. Do not use it with finished-time words (yesterday, last year).

affirmative: We have lived here for five years.
Shan sano ayaan halkan ku noolaannay (wali waan ku nool nahay).
question: Have you eaten?
Wax ma cuntay?
Has she arrived?
Ma timid?
wh: How long have you lived here?
Muddo intee le' ayaad halkan ku nooshahay?

examples: I have finished my homework.
She has lost her key.
We have lived here for five years.
mistakes: I have seen him yesterday → I saw him yesterday
She has went → She has gone
mistakesSo: “Yesterday” waa waqti dhammaaday; isticmaal Past Simple: “I saw him yesterday”.
Present Perfect wuxuu u baahan yahay past participle; qaabka saxda ah waa “has gone”.

title: Present Perfect Continuous
source: original, authored for NORA; Somali needs native review
somali: Waxaa loo isticmaalaa wax bilaabmay waagii hore oo wali socda ama hadda dhawaan dhammaaday, iyadoo la muujinayo muddada. Hab-dhismeedku waa have/has + been + verb-ing. Af-Soomaaliga badanaa waxaa lagu fahmaa macnaha, sidaa darteed qaabkan si gaar ah u baro.
explanation: Use it for actions that started in the past and continue now, with for/since, or recent activity with a visible result.

affirmative: I have been studying for two hours.
Laba saac ayaan wax baranayay (wali waan wax baranayaa).
She has been waiting since morning.
They have been working here since 2020.

examples: I have been studying for two hours.
She has been waiting since morning.

mistakes: I am studying since two hours → I have been studying for two hours
for/since mixed: for two hours, since 2020
mistakesSo: Muddada laba saacadood ah waxaa la raaciyaa “for”, waxaana halkan ku habboon “have been studying”.
“For” waxaa lala adeegsadaa muddo (for two hours); “since” waxaa lala adeegsadaa bilowga waqtiga (since 2020).

title: Past Simple
source: original, authored for NORA; Somali needs native review
somali: Past Simple wuxuu sheegayaa wax dhammaaday waqti hore la yaqaan (shalay, sannadkii hore). Verb-yada caadiga ah waxaa lagu daraa -ed; kuwa aan caadiga ahayn way kala duwan yihiin (go → went). Su'aalaha iyo diidmada waxaa la isticmaalaa did + verb-ka asalka ah.
explanation: Use it for finished actions at a known time in the past. Regular verbs: -ed. Irregular verbs must be learned. Questions and negatives use did + base verb.
formula: Subject + verb-ed / irregular past. Negative: did not + base verb. Question: Did + subject + base verb?

affirmative: We watched a film last night.
question: Did you see him?
Ma aragtay?
Did she come?
Ma timid?

examples: I visited my aunt yesterday.
She bought a new phone.
We watched a film last night.
mistakes: I didn't went → I didn't go
mistakesSo: Ka dib “didn’t” isticmaal falka asalka ah: “go”, ee ha isticmaalin “went”.
“Go” waa fal aan caadi ahayn; Past Simple-kiisu waa “went”.

exercises.explain: Past simple of go is went.

title: Past Perfect

somali: Past Perfect wuxuu sheegayaa wax dhacay ka hor wax kale oo hore u dhacay ("Markaan imid, basku wuu tegey"). Hab-dhismeedku waa had + qaybta saddexaad ee verb-ka.
explanation: Use it for the earlier of two past events. Had + past participle.

affirmative: When I arrived, the bus had left.
Markaan imid, basku horay ayuu u tegey.

negative: I hadn't seen that film before.

mistakes: The bus left when I arrived (earlier action) → had left
mistakesSo: Ficilka dhacay marka hore wuxuu qaataa Past Perfect: “had left”.
“Had” waxaa raaca past participle; “go” past participle-kiisu waa “gone”.

title: Future Simple
